How to Measure Your Bra Size at Home

A simple, step-by-step guide to finding your perfect fit – no fitting room required.

📅 Updated: August 2026 ⏱️ 6 min read

Let's be honest – finding a bra that fits perfectly can feel like searching for a unicorn. One size fits great in one brand but feels completely different in another. And if you're like most women, you've probably been wearing the wrong size for years without realizing it.

In fact, research shows that 38% of women are unsure if they're wearing the correct bra size. And up to 80% of women are wearing the wrong size. The good news? You can fix this in just a few minutes at home.

This guide will walk you through everything you need to know – from measuring your band and bust to calculating your cup size and avoiding common mistakes. Let's get started!

💡 Want to skip the math? Use our Bra Size Calculator – just enter your measurements and we'll do the rest.

What You'll Need

Before you start, gather these simple items:

  • A soft measuring tape – the kind used for sewing, not a hardware store tape measure
  • A mirror – to check that the tape stays level across your back
  • A non-padded or lightly lined bra – wearing this while measuring gives the most accurate results
  • Paper and pen – or your phone, to record your measurements

Pro tip: Avoid measuring over thick clothing or padded bras – they add volume and throw off your numbers.

Step 1: Measure Your Band Size

Your band size is the foundation of your bra. A well-fitted band provides about 80% of the support for your breasts.

How to measure:

  1. Stand up straight with your arms at your sides.
  2. Wrap the measuring tape around your ribcage, directly under your bust.
  3. Keep the tape snug but not tight – it should feel firm against your skin.
  4. Make sure the tape is level – not slanted up or down.
  5. Breathe out normally and take the measurement.

How to calculate your band size:

  • Round your measurement to the nearest whole number.
  • If the number is even, add 4 inches.
  • If the number is odd, add 5 inches.

For example:

  • Underbust: 32" → 32 + 4 = 36 band
  • Underbust: 31" → 31 + 5 = 36 band

Common mistake: Pulling the tape too tight or too loose. It should be snug but comfortable – you should be able to slide two fingers under the tape.

If you're still unsure about your band, try our Band Size Calculator for a quick check.

Step 2: Measure Your Bust Size

Your bust measurement determines your cup letter – the difference between your bust and band size gives you your cup size.

How to measure:

  1. Stand up straight with your arms at your sides.
  2. Wrap the measuring tape around the fullest part of your bust – usually across the nipples.
  3. Keep the tape loose – don't pull it tight or compress your breast tissue.
  4. Make sure the tape is level around your back.
  5. Take the measurement while breathing normally.

Pro tip: Take two or three measurements and use the average for the most accurate result.

For a more precise cup calculation, try our Cup Size Calculator.

Step 3: Calculate Your Cup Size

Now that you have both numbers, it's time to find your cup letter.

The formula is simple:

Cup Size = Bust Measurement – Band Measurement

Difference Cup Size
0 – ½ inchAA
1 inchA
2 inchesB
3 inchesC
4 inchesD
5 inchesDD / E
6 inchesDDD / F
7 inchesG
8 inchesH
9 inchesI
10 inchesJ

Example:

  • Bust: 38 inches
  • Band: 34 inches
  • Difference: 38 – 34 = 4 inches
  • Your size: 34D

For a complete size breakdown, visit our Bra Size Calculator.

Step 4: Put It All Together

Your full bra size is band size + cup size.

For example, if your band is 34 inches and your cup is D, your size is 34D.

Common Measuring Mistakes

Mistake Solution
Tape too tightPull snugly but don't stretch – you should feel it but not be uncomfortable
Tape too looseThe tape should not slip down when you move
Tape not levelUse a mirror to check that the tape runs straight across your back
Measuring over clothesRemove thick tops and padded bras – measure directly over your skin or a non-padded bra
Only measuring onceTake 2-3 measurements and use the average for the most accurate result
Ignoring sister sizesIf your size feels off, try sister sizes – go up one band and down one cup, or vice versa

What If You're Between Sizes?

It's completely normal to be between sizes – especially if you're measuring for the first time. Here's what to do:

  • If the band feels too tight: Try going up one band size and down one cup size (sister size).
  • If the band feels too loose: Try going down one band size and up one cup size (sister size).

For example, if 34C feels a bit tight in the band, try 36B – it has the same cup volume but a looser band.

Use our Sister Size Calculator to find your perfect match instantly.

How Often Should You Measure?

Your body changes over time – weight changes, pregnancy, aging, and even exercise can affect your bra size. We recommend measuring yourself:

  • Every 6 months – for general maintenance
  • Before buying new bras – especially from a brand you haven't tried before
  • After significant weight changes – whether you've gained or lost
  • During pregnancy and nursing – your size can change month to month

If you're pregnant, try our Maternity Bra Calculator for specialized sizing.

Quick Recap – The 3-Step Process

  1. Measure your underbust – snugly under your bust
  2. Measure your bust – loosely around the fullest part
  3. Calculate your size – difference = cup letter, band = rounded +4/+5

That's it! You now know how to measure your bra size at home like a pro.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I measure my bra size by myself?

Yes! The steps above are designed for solo measurement. A mirror helps you keep the tape level.

What if I don't have a measuring tape?

You can use a piece of string or a cord, mark it, and then measure it against a ruler. A sewing measuring tape is easiest, but not essential.

Should I wear a bra while measuring?

Yes – wearing a non-padded or lightly lined bra gives the most accurate measurements for both band and bust.

Why do I get different sizes in different brands?

Each brand uses different fit models and size charts. Your size may vary by brand – that's normal! Always check the brand's size guide and try on when possible.

What are sister sizes?

Sister sizes have the same cup volume but different band and cup letter combinations. For example, 34C → 32D (tighter band) or 36B (looser band). Use our Sister Size Calculator to find yours.

Does IMRango store my measurements?

No. Everything runs locally in your browser. We do not collect, store, or share any of your personal data or measurements.
